short: Formant target and hybrid front end (M06) are standard; evaluation (M12) is behind: random one-second clip split of one speaker, where earlier ultrasound work held out whole utterances.
position: Ultra2Speech [@saha2020ultra2speech] changes the processing stage (M06) twice: a factorized spatial, temporal and joint 3D-convolution front end with channel shuffling, and the first two formants as the acoustic target where 35 of 50 ultrasound-to-speech studies name spectral vocoder parameters (pattern match, Appendix). The front end is standard: spatiotemporal convolution is the most frequent ultrasound front end. The formant target departs from the usual target, as no ledger ultrasound-to-speech study first public before it predicts formants (Appendix); it is rated standard because no spectral-target system is trained on its data (Table 1) and the data are vowel sequences only (Sec. 4.1). Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work on protocol: earlier single-speaker ultrasound-to-acoustic studies held out whole utterances [@hueber2011statistical; @csapo2017dnn; @gosztolya2019autoencoder], while this paper shuffles one-second clips at random and scores only formant regression.
